Verdict: needs_cleaning before training. The dataset is structurally sound (1200 rows x 24 cols, target present with 0% missing and 2 balanced-ish classes 69/31), but three issues block a clean training run.

1) Sentinel/placeholder values in the numeric block. num_feature_04, num_feature_08 and num_feature_12 all have max = 9999.0 while their medians sit at ~54-62 (e.g. num_feature_04 q50 = 54.26). Their stds of 846.2, 828.5 and 824.6 against means of ~126-131 confirm a tiny number of extreme values dominate the moments. 9999 is almost certainly a missing sentinel; mask it to NaN and impute before scaling, otherwise standardisation will be corrupted.

2) Systematic missingness. Non-trivial missing rates appear across many numeric columns (num_feature_04 8.5%, num_feature_09 8.25%, num_feature_14 8.58%, num_feature_13 7.83%) and grow monotonically across the categoricals (cat_feature_01 2.7% -> cat_feature_07 22.1%). The categoricals also have high cardinality (cat_feature_07 31, cat_feature_06 27, cat_feature_05 23, cat_feature_04 19, cat_feature_03 15), so imputing them with a mode constant or one-hot expansion risks both bias and dimensionality blow-up. A missing-indicator plus a principled imputer is safer.

3) Outliers are moderate, not fatal. IQR-based counts are 11-15 for the sentinel-affected columns and z-score counts are 8 for each of num_feature_04/08/12; most other numerics have 1-6. Trimming at this stage is unnecessary - fixing the 9999 sentinel will remove most of the extreme mass.

Recommended checks before training: confirm 9999 is a placeholder (and whether other sentinels like -1 or 0 exist); test whether the missingness pattern is informative (i.e. correlate missing-indicators with the target, since pattern-level structure could make MNAR imputation necessary); verify the signup_date range for temporal leakage and check for duplicate rows. No leakage columns such as IDs are visible, and is_active/signup_date are fully populated.

Bottom line: fix sentinels, choose and document an imputation strategy with missing indicators, then this is ready to train.

Shape and target: 1,200 rows x 24 columns. The target is a binary classification label with cardinality 2 and a moderate class imbalance (0 = 68.9%, 1 = 31.1%), which is workable but should be handled with stratification or class weighting.

Missing values: missingness is pervasive but mostly low-to-moderate. Numeric columns range from 0% (num_feature_05, num_feature_10) up to 8.58% (num_feature_14); num_feature_01 has 2.5% and num_feature_04 8.5%. The categorical block is worse and grows monotonically: cat_feature_04 at 12.7%, cat_feature_05 at 13.9%, cat_feature_06 at 19.5%, and cat_feature_07 at 22.1% — above the 20% mark where naive imputation starts distorting distribution. The profile's own warning flags four columns in the 10-50% missing band. Numeric imputation (median, or model-based) is reasonable, but for the high-missing categoricals consider an explicit "missing"/"unknown" category rather than dropping rows, which would otherwise discard a large share of data.

Sentinel outliers: num_feature_04, num_feature_08 and num_feature_12 all share a suspicious max of exactly 9999.0 against quartiles around 45-70 and stds of ~825-846. This is clearly a placeholder for missing/invalid values, not a real measurement; these must be converted to NaN before any scaling or tree split, otherwise they will dominate distance- and gradient-based learners.

Categorical encoding: cardinality grows with the missingness pattern (cat_feature_07 has 31 levels, cat_feature_06 27, cat_feature_05 23, cat_feature_04 19), so one-hot encoding will be wide and should be replaced by target/ordinal encoding or a hashing scheme, with folds to avoid leakage.

Other notes: is_active and signup_date are complete (0% missing), and signup_date should be parsed to datetime and possibly expanded into temporal features. Outlier counts via IQR/z-score are low to modest (e.g., 12 IQR / 6 z for num_feature_01), so genuine outliers are not the main concern — the sentinels are.

Recommended path: replace 9999 sentinels with NaN, choose and document an imputation strategy per column type, encode high-cardinality categoricals carefully, stratify on target, and re-profile before training.

Missingness is widespread: 9 numeric columns carry 1.4%-8.6% missing (num_feature_14 at 0.0858, num_feature_04 at 0.085, num_feature_09 at 0.0825), and the categorical block degrades monotonically from cat_feature_01 (2.7% missing, 7 levels) up to cat_feature_07 (22.1% missing, 31 levels), with cat_feature_04/cat_feature_05/cat_feature_06 also in the 12.7%-19.5% band. High-cardinality categoricals at high missing rates need a deliberate strategy (drop-if-high-missing / target or frequency encoding / explicit "missing" level) rather than naive one-hot, while low-cardinality cat_feature_01/cat_feature_02 are safe to impute and one-hot. The binary target is clean (0% missing, 2 classes, ~69/31 imbalance) and is_active/signup_date are complete, so the label and a few features are trustworthy. Recommended: fix the 9999 sentinels, choose per-column imputation for the 4+ columns in the 10-50% missing band, cap or encode the high-cardinality categoricals, and validate outliers flagged by the IQR counts (up to 15 per numeric column) before training.

The data is not ready to train yet; it needs cleaning first. The dominant issue is a sentinel-value contamination: num_feature_04, num_feature_08 and num_feature_12 all share max = 9999.0 while their stds (846.24, 828.49, 824.59) are ~70x the stds of the other numeric features (~12), and their means (~127-131) sit far above their medians (~54-62). That pattern is a classic missing-value code, not real signal, so those values must be dropped or masked before scaling/imputation. Missingness is also widespread: four numeric features sit in the 4-9% range (num_feature_12 3.75%, num_feature_08 4.58%, num_feature_04 8.5%, num_feature_14 8.58%), while four categoricals are worse (cat_feature_04 12.67%, cat_feature_05 13.92%, cat_feature_06 19.5%, cat_feature_07 22.08%); at 19.5%/22.08% a separate "missing" indicator or careful imputation is warranted rather than blind mode-fill. High-cardinality categoricals (cat_feature_07 with 31 levels, plus the neighbouring 19-27 level features) will need encoding that tolerates rare levels. On the positive side, the binary target is fully populated (cardinality 2) with a workable 69/31 split, the date column is complete, and the outlier counts (IQR 7-15, z-score 1-8) are modest once the 9999 sentinels are removed. Recommended: treat 9999 as missing, then re-profile, choose imputation, and encode categoricals before training.
